Keep the marker outside the subagent-writable tree (e.g. under `.run/` or mktemp) or record a hash of it in the session.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:458 — The scope check compares `git status --porcelain` lines only, so edits to files that were already dirty (` M` stays ` M`) and edits to existing ignored files (`!!` stays `!!`) are invisible. Ignored files include grimoires/loa/prd.md, sdd.md, NOTES.md and the priority-1 hand-off snapshots `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md`. A research subagent can rewrite a PRD or another map's "settled decisions" snapshot and research-end still passes. Compare content hashes, not status lines.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:71 — Same flaw in the unblock probe: a status-line diff does not catch a probe that modifies an already-modified tracked file or an existing ignored file (.beads/, .run/, grimoires/loa/prd.md). The detached worktree also shares refs, config, hooks and stash with the main repository (line 58/66), so a probe can create or delete branches or tags, or rewrite .git/config and hooks, without any status change. The comment's promise that "the main tree's status changed" fails the ticket does not hold for these writes.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:437 — The dispatch marker `.chart-${SLUG}-${TICKET}.dispatch` and report `chart-${SLUG}-${TICKET}.md` are ambiguous because both slugs may contain `-`: map `a` + ticket `b-c` and map `a-b` + ticket `c` collide on the same marker and report. The cap glob `.chart-${SLUG}-*.dispatch` (line 444) also counts dispatches of every map whose slug starts with `${SLUG}-` (map `eval` counts `eval-workers` tickets).
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:379 — The handoff glob `chart-${SLUG}-*.md` inlines research reports that belong to a different map whose slug has this slug as a prefix (map `eval` pulls in `chart-eval-workers-*.md`) into this map's priority-1 snapshot.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:433 — `close` (and `--consumed-by` in particular) leaves `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<slug>.md` in place. `golden_resolve_open_map --snapshots` (golden-path.sh:114) builds its candidates from snapshot files without looking at the map's Status, so a consumed or abandoned map is re-offered and re-ingested as priority-1 "settled" context by every later /plan-and-analyze. Once two maps have ever been consumed, an unattended /plan-and-analyze stops forever with "more than one open map: name one". Remove the snapshot on close, or filter candidates by map Status.
head/.claude/commands/plan-and-analyze.md:50 — The pre-existing priority-2 `grimoires/loa/context/*.md` glob (and the new priority-1 `chart-*.md` glob at line 44) loads every hand-off snapshot. That includes the ones not chosen by the multi-map rule and stale snapshots of closed maps, which contradicts "Other snapshots are not ingested" (line 190). Exclude `chart-*.md` from the generic glob and load only the resolved snapshot.
head/.claude/scripts/golden-path.sh:94 — `_gp_is_unattended` fails open. When dec-write-lib.sh is installed but `context` errors, prints nothing or prints anything other than `unattended`, the context counts as interactive (LOA_UNATTENDED is consulted only for empty output), and `--prd` is not passed, so the autonomous PRD Status signal that chart-guard.sh uses is not consulted. An unattended run then gets rc 3 ("ask the operator") instead of rc 1. chart-guard.sh:41 deliberately fails closed; this helper should too.
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:172 — `epic` is not idempotent, unlike the rest of the write-order contract. The bead is created before the map doc, and a re-run looks only for the doc (line 161). An interruption or failure between `br create` and the `mv` at line 195 (e.g. mktemp or mkdir failing) leaves an orphan `map` epic, and the re-run creates a second one. Look up an existing epic by label `map` and slug `map-<slug>` before creating.

head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5 — `Bash(br *)` / `br ["*"]` gives the skill unrestricted br (create `--type task`, `label add sprint:…`, `dep`, `delete`), while the objective (line 65) says it "never creates a task bead and never adds a sprint: label" and claims enforcement. Only the post-hoc validator catches this. Narrow it to the br subcommands the flow needs, or drop the claim.
head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5 — The dispatching skill declares `web_access: false` (SKILL.md:40) but spawns a write-capable agent with WebFetch and an unrestricted Write tool. The skill's capability declaration is escalated through `agent_spawn`, and fetched web text flows into tracked reports that are inlined into the priority-1 hand-off snapshot. Declare web access on the skill, or scope it explicitly.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:845 — The SP-1 checkout path-copy check treats only positional operands as copies. `git checkout -p spike/x` (hunks copied from the spike into the working tree) and `git checkout spike/x --pathspec-from-file=list` pass, even though they are the same "copy content out of a spike" that the rule claims to block. Neither is in the listed "Misses".
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:654 — The D-5.9 delete allowance requires a decided row whose `source` is `grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md`. A `decision:prototype` ticket charted through /chart resolves its own row, whose source is `map:<slug>/<ticket>` (chart-ticket.sh:218/306). So a map-originated spike's verdict never unlocks `git branch -D spike/<slug>` unless a second, duplicate row is written. Neither SKILL.md:136-139 nor REFERENCE.md describes which row the verdict goes on.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 18 findings, verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I didn't change anything under `pr/`.

**The checks meant to stop out-of-scope writes can be bypassed. These are the main reasons it can't merge:**
- **Research check can be faked.** The file holding the "before" snapshot sits in `grimoires/loa/research/`, the one folder the research subagent may write to. That folder is also exempt from the check, so the subagent can overwrite the snapshot and pass both checks.
- **Some edits are invisible.** The research check and `chart-unblock-probe.sh` compare only `git status` lines. They miss edits to files that were already modified and to existing gitignored files. That covers `prd.md`, `NOTES.md` and the hand-off snapshots `/plan-and-analyze` reads as settled decisions.
- **The probe can still change the main repo.** Its throwaway worktree shares branches, tags, config and hooks with the main checkout, and changing those never shows up in `git status`.

**Workflow bugs:**
- **Closing a map leaves its snapshot behind.** That snapshot is re-read as "settled decisions" by every later `/plan-and-analyze`. Once two maps have been closed, unattended runs stop permanently with "more than one open map". Separately, the generic `context/*.md` glob loads every snapshot anyway, despite the doc saying unchosen ones are skipped.
- **Unattended detection in `golden-path.sh` fails open.** If the context check errors, the run is treated as interactive. `chart-guard.sh` deliberately treats the same case as unattended.
- **Names can collide.** Map and ticket slugs may both contain hyphens, so research files can collide across maps. Map `eval` also counts and pulls in `eval-workers`' research.
- **`chart-ticket.sh epic` isn't safe to re-run.** If it's interrupted after creating the epic, a re-run creates a second epic.
- **Tickets from a linked worktree fail validation.** `chart-ticket.sh` accepts `PEND-` row ids there, but the map validator only accepts `DEC-` ids.
- **Decision tickets can still leak into build work.** `get-ready-work.sh` filters on `.issue_type` only, while every other component also checks `.type`.
- **`--root` is not fully respected.** It still pulls rows from the real checkout's pending ledgers.

**Lower-severity:**
- **The skill's own rules block one of its steps.** It tells the agent to `source golden-path.sh`, which its command allowlist doesn't permit.
- **`Bash(br *)` is too broad.** It contradicts the claim that the skill never creates task beads or sprint labels.
- **The research agent has web access the skill says it doesn't.** It can fetch web pages, while the skill declares `web_access: false`.
- **The spike-copy hook misses two copy forms:** `git checkout -p spike/x` and `--pathspec-from-file`.
- **Spikes from `/chart` can't be cleaned up.** Their verdict is recorded on the map row, not the spikes-file row the branch-delete rule looks for, so `git branch -D` stays blocked.

I couldn't run the PR's bats suites. In a copy of the head tree they fail at setup because the libraries they depend on (`dec-write-lib.sh`, `bootstrap.sh`, `compat-lib.sh`) aren't in this snapshot. I did run the hook directly against about 50 command strings, which is how I confirmed the two spike-copy gaps.
